input.message: What is spectral resolving power and how high is it for SPHEREx?

expected.behavior: Define dimensionless R = lambda/delta_lambda, give the nominal detector values, and avoid saying all narrow emission is undetectable. Name the source; no observation-data tool is needed.
expected.reference_answer: Spectral resolving power is R = lambda/delta_lambda and is dimensionless. IRSA gives nominal R values of 39, 41, 41, 35, 112 and 128 for SPHEREx detector bands 1-6. Features narrower than the instrumental bandwidth cannot be individually resolved; broad features may be measured if the signal-to-noise is sufficient.

input.message: What is the SPHEREx All-Sky Cube?

expected.behavior: Describe 102 channels while acknowledging the blank channels and FITS-versus-PNG distinction. Do not promise valid data in every sky pixel or channel. Name the source; no observation-data tool is needed.
expected.reference_answer: The DR1 All-Sky Cube combines spectral images into sky tiles with 102 spectral channels. It has zodiacal light subtracted, unlike the Level 2 IMAGE layer. input.message: There are no SPHEREx images of this position for five months between two visits. Does that mean nothing changed?

expected.behavior: Absence of images does not establish constancy or necessarily prove the position was not observed. Check archive release, query constraints, quality rejection and ingestion delays before asserting an observing gap.
expected.reference_answer: No. A missing image does not show that the source stayed constant. It may mean the position was not observed, but it can also reflect release coverage, filtering, quality rejection or ingestion delays. Check query constraints and archive coverage before calling it a true observing gap. Source: IRSA SPHEREx data access and product documentation.

input.message: I saw a dot move between two SPHEREx images. Did I discover a new brown dwarf?

expected.behavior: Treat apparent motion as an unconfirmed candidate; discuss alignment, artifacts, known objects, catalog checks and independent follow-up. Do not imply a particular Q-FIT review state or successful submission without implementation evidence.
expected.reference_answer: This is a candidate that needs investigation. Apparent motion can come from alignment errors, artifacts or a known moving object. Compare astrometry, observing times, bandpasses and catalogs; then seek independent review and appropriate follow-up observations. Brown dwarf identity and any discovery claim need additional evidence. Source: the Backyard Worlds candidate and follow-up workflow described by JPL.
